81aa3344ff.q: How can remote engineering teams maintain trust and presence without requiring cameras on at all times?
81aa3344ff.a: Helen conducted a trial where her team turned cameras off for 10-15 minutes and found after seven minutes that the product person said they needed cameras back on—the meeting became substantially better when video was enabled. She notes that 70-80% of communication happens through body language and tone beyond words alone. However, she acknowledges some engineers strongly dislike being on camera and that it can feel more vulnerable than in-person presence. The key is finding team agreement: in one company, Helen's policy was cameras on unless eating or unwell, as it helps with presence and understanding.

82f545d17a.q: How do engineering leaders transition teams from individual objectives to collective team goals?
82f545d17a.a: Helen explains that teams need clear team objectives—typically the top three goals for a sprint or iteration. When people understand the implications and business impact, they're more willing to pause individual work to support critical deliverables. Leaders should facilitate peer reviews and ensure fair collaboration so senior engineers don't burn out covering junior engineers' work. The key is communication: leaders must explicitly discuss workload balance, let team members voice concerns when collaboration isn't flowing well, and help everyone see that the team's delivery depends on mutual support, not just individual contribution.

06359a1815.q: Why is Slight Reliability podcast ending after four and a half years and 125 episodes?
06359a1815.a: The host decided to end the podcast because they have been producing two podcasts simultaneously alongside their day job, family commitments, and other hobbies, which has stretched them too thin. While creating Slight Reliability has been an act of love and obligation to the community, it requires significant time and energy. The host is choosing to focus on Tales from the Humpback Sky instead, a collaborative creative project that feeds their energy and provides a counterbalance to their career work.
